models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Pre-trip look: dead-calm pattern over the Aeolians, 1-6 kt and near-flat seas - but the trip dates are still out of range.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the islands at the moment - the consensus across all available models (sampled every 6 h) gives 1-6 kt with seas 0.1-0.4 ft everywhere from Portorosa to Filicudi. Direction is doing what it does in a slack pattern: light southerlies overnight at Portorosa backing to NE/E by midday, and a persistent N to NE drift of 3-5 kt around Lipari, Panarea and Stromboli with an evening freshening to 5-6 kt. ECMWF IFS (29 Sep 00Z), ECMWF AIFS (29 Sep 06Z) and ICON-2i (29 Sep 00Z) all agree on the light-air picture; the one flagged split is Portorosa on the night of 1 Oct, where the models spread 1.0-7.7 kt. If this held, the fleet would be motoring more than sailing.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the night of 3 Oct at Portorosa, the recommendation is Portorosa Marina - an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, and the only listed option there, so the choice does not matter. The current forecast for that night is 3 kt ESE, gusts 8.7 kt, swell 0.1 ft: nothing that would push the fleet anywhere. Bear in mind that night is still four days out and the scoring will be re-run as it comes into range.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: This is a pre-trip outlook rather than a departure briefing, so there is no next-morning window to call yet. For the first leg on 4 Oct the payload's recommended departure is 06:00, with all windows from 06:00 to 14:00 scored 'go' and no deterioration flagged. Treat that as a placeholder: it is at the edge of the forecast reach (05 Oct 23:00) and will shift.

passage_notes.note: Currently 'go' all day; 06:00 gives 5.9 kt SSE, gusts 11.5 kt, 0.1 ft sea - a run under 3 hours. Wind backs to NE by midday for a close reach. Expect to motor.
'Go', but 3-3.5 kt from the NE and NNE puts the breeze on the nose - head to wind, motoring passage. Seas 0.1 ft. At the very end of the forecast horizon.
'Go' on current data, 3-3.9 kt N/NNE, 0.1 ft. Marina del Gabbiano scores only 'workable' - open from every direction, no anchoring - so it relies on the calm holding.

passage_notes.leg: Panarea → Filicudi, Filicudi → Salina and later legs
passage_notes.note: Beyond the 05 Oct forecast reach. No forecast exists for these dates; the dry-run scores in the payload are yesterday's weather on tomorrow's route, not a forecast.

cautions: Portorosa overnight 1 Oct: models disagree badly, 1.0-7.7 kt. That is a spread, not a mean - relevant only as a sign the pattern is weakly defined.
Marina del Gabbiano (Stromboli) is rated 'workable', exposed through the full 360° with no anchoring. Shelter there depends entirely on the calm persisting, and that is unforecastable at this range.

Direction is the unstable element: forecast stability at 72-120 h lead shows a mean direction shift of 65° between runs, against a mean wind-speed shift of only 0.7 kt. Plan on the strength, not the heading.
Verdicts shown are conservative threshold outputs, not decisions - the skipper decides on the day.
briefing.confidence_note: The three wind models agree closely on a benign, light-air regime and run-to-run wind-speed shifts are under 1 kt, but direction swings 65° on average at this lead and most of the itinerary sits past the 05 Oct forecast horizon, so nothing here should be taken as a forecast for the trip dates.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
